codeTemplates.summary: Argues CPT 19380 revision surgery is medically necessary correction of a prior reconstructive complication, not a cosmetic re-do, and is not excluded by the provider contract.
codeTemplates.body:
To Whom It May Concern:

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}

We are writing to formally appeal the denial of CPT 19380 (revision of reconstructed breast) performed by {{Provider.Name}} for our patient, {{Patient.Name}}, on {{Claim.ServiceDate}}. {{Payer.Name}} denied this claim as non-covered under the provider contract; we respectfully disagree, as this determination mischaracterizes a medically necessary revision as an excluded or elective service.

CPT 19380 describes surgical correction of a complication of prior breast reconstruction — including but not limited to asymmetry requiring surgical correction, capsular contracture, flap or implant malposition, contour irregularity causing functional or symptomatic compromise, or a partial reconstructive failure. [DESCRIBE: specific clinical indication for this revision — e.g. capsular contracture grade, documented asymmetry, flap complication]. This is corrective, reconstructive surgery performed to remedy a documented complication of a covered reconstructive procedure, not an elective cosmetic enhancement, and falls squarely within the reconstructive-surgery coverage mandated for post-mastectomy patients under the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act (WHCRA) and under {{Payer.Name}}'s own reconstructive-surgery coverage policy.

The operative report and clinical documentation enclosed with this appeal establish the specific complication being corrected, the medical necessity of surgical intervention, and that this revision was not requested for purely aesthetic reasons. [FILL IN: brief note on any prior conservative management attempted, if applicable].

We respectfully request that {{Payer.Name}}:
• Review the enclosed operative report and clinical documentation confirming the reconstructive (not cosmetic) nature of this revision.
• Overturn the non-covered denial and reprocess CPT 19380 as a covered reconstructive service.
• Confirm in writing the specific contract provision relied upon if any portion of this appeal is not granted in full.

We expect a formal redetermination within standard appeal timelines. For any immediate clinical or administrative inquiries regarding this appeal, contact {{Sender.Name}} directly at {{Sender.Email}} or {{Sender.Phone}}.

codeTemplates.summary: Same CPT 19380 revision argument, framed against a patient-plan exclusion determination rather than a provider-contract denial.
codeTemplates.body:
To Whom It May Concern:

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}

We are appealing the denial of CPT 19380, revision of reconstructed breast, performed by {{Provider.Name}} for {{Patient.Name}} on {{Claim.ServiceDate}}, which {{Payer.Name}} denied as not covered under the patient's benefit plan.

Federal law under the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act (WHCRA) of 1998 requires group health plans that cover mastectomy to also cover reconstruction of the affected breast and surgery/reconstruction of the other breast to produce a symmetrical appearance, as well as treatment of physical complications at all stages of mastectomy, including reconstructive revision. This federal mandate applies regardless of whether the plan document separately lists CPT 19380 by name — a plan cannot exclude medically necessary correction of a reconstructive complication when it covers the underlying mastectomy and initial reconstruction. [DESCRIBE: specific complication being corrected and why it required surgical revision].

We request that {{Payer.Name}} review this denial against its WHCRA obligations and reprocess this claim as a covered reconstructive service, not an excluded procedure.

We respectfully request that {{Payer.Name}}:
• Confirm whether the patient's plan is subject to WHCRA (all group health plans providing mastectomy coverage are).
• Overturn the denial and reprocess CPT 19380 consistent with WHCRA reconstructive-coverage requirements.
• Provide the specific plan exclusion language relied upon, in writing, if this appeal is not granted in full.

We expect a formal redetermination within standard appeal timelines. For any immediate clinical or administrative inquiries regarding this appeal, contact {{Sender.Name}} directly at {{Sender.Email}} or {{Sender.Phone}}.

codeTemplates.summary: Argues CPT 19380 was correctly and safely performed in an accredited in-office setting (POS 11), citing the CMS Physician Fee Schedule non-facility RVU as regulatory support.
codeTemplates.body:

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}

This letter serves as a formal appeal to contest the denial of CPT 19380 (revision of reconstructed breast) under Claim #{{Claim.Number}}, which was denied based on an invalid Place of Service determination. We respectfully request full reconsideration, acceptance of the billed place of service, and reprocessing of the claim for payment.

Clinical Summary and Medical Necessity: [DESCRIBE: the specific acquired deformity or complication of the prior reconstruction being corrected — e.g. contour irregularity, asymmetry, capsular contracture — and confirm this was a corrective, non-cosmetic revision]. The procedure was performed under local anesthesia in an accredited office setting, with excision of the affected tissue, hemostasis, and layered closure, without complication.

Justification for the Billed Place of Service: This procedure was performed entirely within the physician's accredited office environment, utilizing local anesthesia without requiring hospital or ambulatory surgical center overhead resources. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Physician Fee Schedule establishes a valid non-facility (office) relative value unit (RVU) for CPT 19380, explicitly recognizing that the AMA and CMS anticipate and permit this code to be safely and appropriately performed in a properly equipped office setting. [DESCRIBE: if prior authorization #{{Claim.AuthNumber}} was active and did not restrict place of service, note that here]. Denying the claim based on a perceived place-of-service restriction contradicts the non-facility pricing indicator and the clinical feasibility of this minor outpatient revision.

The services rendered were medically necessary, properly authorized, correctly coded, and safely performed in an appropriate office environment.

We respectfully request that you overturn the denial, accept the billed place of service as correct, and reprocess Claim #{{Claim.Number}} for prompt payment. Should you require any additional documentation or clinical clarification, please contact {{Sender.Name}} directly at {{Sender.Email}} or {{Sender.Phone}}.

codeTemplates.summary: Argues CPT 19364 was incorrectly flagged as a duplicate of a co-surgeon's or the same-day claim, when it represents distinct, separately reportable microsurgical work — includes contracted per-surgeon-per-side rate and PA-not-credentialed billing explanation.
codeTemplates.body:
To Whom It May Concern:

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}
Diagnosis Code(s): {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}}

We are appealing the denial of CPT 19364 as a duplicate claim or service. This determination is incorrect. CPT 19364 (breast reconstruction with free flap, e.g. DIEP/TRAM) was performed by {{Provider.Name}} as a distinct, medically necessary microsurgical reconstructive procedure — it was not billed twice for the same operative work.

[DESCRIBE: if a co-surgeon performed this procedure with modifier -62, or if bilateral reconstruction was performed with modifiers -LT/-RT, cite that here]. Free-flap breast reconstruction frequently involves two operating surgeons working simultaneously on the same reconstructive episode — one managing flap harvest, the other managing recipient-site preparation and microvascular anastomosis — each independently and fully engaged throughout the procedure, which is correctly billed with co-surgeon modifier -62 on each surgeon's own claim rather than as a duplicate of the other's. Our contracted reimbursement structure for CPT 19364 is per-surgeon, per-side: {{Provider.Name}}'s primary-side rate is [FILL IN: primary-side contracted rate] and the assisting-side rate is [FILL IN: assist-side contracted rate], for a total contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} — this claim should be reviewed and reimbursed in full alignment with that applicable contractual agreement.

[DESCRIBE: if any portion of this claim reflects assistant-at-surgery work by a Physician Assistant who is not independently credentialed with {{Payer.Name}}]. Where our employed PA is not independently credentialed with {{Payer.Name}}, assistant services are necessarily billed under the supervising surgeon's own NPI using the standard assistant-at-surgery modifier — this administrative billing structure can cause the PA's separately-billed assistant claim to be mistaken for a duplicate of the primary surgeon's claim for the same encounter; they are two distinct, separately reimbursable services.

Claim #{{Claim.Number}} reflects a single, complete, and non-duplicative episode of medically necessary reconstructive surgery. We request that {{Payer.Name}} review the operative report, which documents the specific role performed by {{Provider.Name}} and confirms this was not a repeat billing of an already-adjudicated service.

We respectfully request that {{Payer.Name}}:
• Review the operative report confirming the distinct surgical role and/or laterality of the billed service.
• Overturn the duplicate denial and reprocess CPT 19364 for payment at the full contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}}.
• Identify the specific claim {{Payer.Name}} believes this duplicates, in writing, if any portion remains denied.

We expect a formal redetermination within standard appeal timelines. For any immediate clinical or administrative inquiries regarding this appeal, contact {{Sender.Name}} directly at {{Sender.Email}} or {{Sender.Phone}}.

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}
Diagnosis Code(s): {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}}

This correspondence serves as a formal appeal and request for reconsideration of assistant-at-surgery services billed under CPT 55970-AS, denied under Remark/Group Code PR-96 ("Non-covered charge"), in connection with the complex gender-affirming genital reconstruction performed by {{Provider.Name}}. We respectfully dispute this determination based on approved prior authorization, established medical necessity, documented necessity of a non-physician surgical assistant, and applicable payer reimbursement guidelines.

Billing Methodology & Credentialing Compliance: Per standard payer reimbursement guidelines, when a Certified Physician Assistant (PA-C) is not individually credentialed with the payer's network at the time of service, assistant-at-surgery services are properly billed under the supervising primary surgeon's NPI using modifier -AS (non-physician assistant at surgery). The claim line reflects the distinct surgical-assistant allowance for the PA-C and does not represent a duplicate or non-covered service — denying this line under PR-96 fails to recognize standard coding conventions for non-credentialed surgical assistants performing authorized surgical cases.

Clinical Complexity & Documented Assistant Necessity: CPT 55970 represents an extraordinarily complex, multi-step anatomical reconstruction. [DESCRIBE: specific operative components performed, e.g. dissection, allograft/skin-graft placement, tissue reduction and multi-layer closure]. [DESCRIBE: if the operative note documents that no qualified surgical resident was available for this case, and that the extreme clinical complexity, extensive dissection, and continuous deep-tissue retraction required throughout the procedure could not safely be performed with only one pair of hands].

Prior Authorization & Medical Necessity Alignment: {{Payer.Name}} evaluated and formally approved the primary procedure (CPT 55970) as medically necessary under Prior Authorization #{{Claim.AuthNumber}}. Accepted clinical standards from WPATH (Version 8) and the American Medical Association confirm gender-affirming genital reconstruction as non-elective, medically necessary care — denying surgical-assistant coverage for an authorized, high-complexity procedure directly conflicts with {{Payer.Name}}'s own prior approval and patient-safety standards.

Demand for Specific Policy Disclosure: If {{Payer.Name}} maintains that CPT 55970 is excluded from assistant-at-surgery reimbursement despite prior authorization approval for the primary procedure, we request the exact member benefit plan contract language stating that CPT 55970 is excluded from assistant-at-surgery reimbursement, and the specific code-editing rules or fee-schedule restrictions stating CPT 55970 cannot be billed with modifier -AS for a PA-C.

We respectfully request that {{Payer.Name}}:
• Reopen and re-adjudicate this claim.
• Overturn the PR-96 non-covered-charge denial for CPT 55970-AS.
• Process payment for the non-physician assistant-at-surgery services billed under {{Provider.Name}}'s profile with modifier -AS.

We expect a formal redetermination within standard appeal timelines. For any immediate clinical or administrative inquiries regarding this appeal, contact {{Sender.Name}} directly at {{Sender.Email}} or {{Sender.Phone}}.

archetypes.name: Assistant Surgeon — PA Not Credentialed, Billed Under Main Surgeon
denialCategories: NPI or Non Par or Out of Network
archetypes.summary: Core PA/Assistant scenario: since the PA isn't independently credentialed with the payer, services were billed under the main surgeon with the AS modifier. Argues consistency — the payer already paid the primary surgeon claim for the same operative session, so the assistant claim can't be denied on medical necessity/coverage grounds.
archetypes.body:
To Whom It May Concern:

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}

We are submitting this Formal Provider-Level Appeal on behalf of {{Provider.Name}} and {{Practice.Name}}, regarding the denial of assistant surgeon services rendered by our employed Physician Assistant, {{Assistant.Name}}. These services were provided during a complex, medically necessary reconstructive surgery performed on our patient, {{Patient.Name}}, on {{Claim.ServiceDate}} at [FILL IN: facility name].

[IF APPLICABLE: reference the payer's latest determination notice date and boilerplate denial language, and any timely-filing compliance argument with DCN/confirmation number.]

The denial of assistant surgeon services ignores the structural and operational realities of provider credentialing and network participation:

Billing Under the Main Surgeon: Our practice, {{Practice.Name}}, is fully credentialed for the primary surgeon ({{Provider.Name}}); however, {{Payer.Name}}'s current credentialing policies do not permit independent or direct billing/credentialing for our employed Physician Assistants under separate group structures for these specific surgical lines. Consequently, the assistant surgeon services provided by {{Assistant.Name}} were correctly billed under the main surgeon's billing entity utilizing the standard assistant-at-surgery modifier (-AS).

Consistency with Paid Primary Claim: {{Payer.Name}} processed, approved, and paid the primary surgeon's claim for this exact surgical encounter. This proves that the plan has already validated the medical necessity, coverage, and contractual validity of the surgical session. Refusing to reimburse the indispensable assistant surgeon services utilized during the exact same operative session is arbitrary and penalizes the practice for standard, compliant billing mechanics.

Clinical Summary
[FILL IN: description of the surgical intervention and why assistant support was medically necessary — complexity, anatomical detail, findings]

[FILL IN, if applicable: itemized rebuttal of any vague denial language, demanding the specific contract provision allegedly breached]

Based on the complete administrative and clinical record, we respectfully demand that {{Payer.Name}} immediately overturn the improper denial and:
• Fully approve and process payment for the appropriately billed assistant surgeon services under CPT {{Claim.CPT}}, remitted directly to {{Practice.Name}}.
• Formally verify TFL compliance, if applicable.
• Escalate this dispute to a qualified medical director or clinical coding specialist with expertise in complex reconstructive surgical billing and assistant-at-surgery guidelines.
• If any portion of this claim is maintained, provide a detailed, itemized written response addressing each disputed CPT code individually and citing explicit contract provisions rather than issuing generalized rejection templates.

We expect a formal redetermination within standard appeal timelines. For any immediate clinical or administrative inquiries regarding this appeal, contact {{Sender.Name}} directly at {{Sender.Email}} or {{Sender.Phone}}.

archetypes.name: Co-Surgeon / Simultaneous Multi-Surgeon Emergency (NSA & MPFS Defense)

archetypes.summary: The most technical archetype: two or more attending surgeons operated simultaneously on separate anatomical fields under one anesthetic, cross-assisting each other. Used when a payer applies PI-54 (multiple physicians/assistants not covered), PR-97 (incidental/bundled), or similar denial codes on lines tied to a co-surgeon or cross-assistance arrangement, especially where the case originated from the Emergency Department (invokes the federal No Surprises Act). Includes a CPT-by-CPT technical defense section.
archetypes.body:

[IF EMERGENCY / ED ORIGIN: These denials are clinically, contractually, and statutorily invalid. Because this patient presented through the Emergency Department at [FILL IN facility] under [FILL IN acute condition] and underwent emergency surgical intervention, this claim is subject to Emergency Services Protections under the Federal No Surprises Act (NSA), combined with the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) framework and AMA CPT coding guidelines.]

Clinical Narrative & Surgical Context
On {{Claim.ServiceDate}}, the patient [FILL IN: presenting condition / diagnosis / findings]. Because of the [emergent / complex] nature of the case and the critical requirement to execute [FILL IN: procedures] under a single anesthetic window, [FILL IN number] attending surgeons ({{Provider.Name}} and [FILL IN co-surgeon name]) operated simultaneously on separate anatomical fields:
[FILL IN: Surgeon A — primary role / field]
[FILL IN: Surgeon B — primary role / field]

Simultaneous multi-field operating is a recognized standard of care for [FILL IN clinical context]. It directly diminishes total operative duration, limits cumulative anesthetic exposure, and mitigates postoperative morbidities. [FOR EACH DISPUTED CPT LINE, FILL IN:]

Regulatory Defense: [explain modifier usage (-59, -80, -78 etc.), why the service is distinct/not incidental, and the clinical basis]

[IF NSA APPLIES:]
Federal No Surprises Act (NSA) Mandate for Emergency Care
Because this patient was admitted and treated under emergency care conditions, this claim falls under the consumer and provider protections of the Federal No Surprises Act:
• Emergency services must be covered without requiring prior authorization and without retrospective administrative barriers or improper bundling that penalizes emergency multi-surgeon coordination.
• Arbitrary assistant denials and improper incidental bundling on emergency cases violate federal network parity and emergency reimbursement standards; the claim must be reprocessed to reflect appropriate emergency-tier reimbursement.

archetypes.name: Per-Surgeon-Per-Side Contract Billing (CPT 19364 Co-Surgeon / PA Confusion)
sourceFiles: PA claim denied as duplicate by CareFirst.docx
Formal Appeal BCBS Carefirst Bilateral Diep.docx
archetypes.summary: The practice's signature CPT 19364 defense: the payer contract pays each surgeon separately per side (LT/RT) rather than with modifier 62, so two co-surgeon claims — or a co-surgeon claim plus a PA assistant-at-surgery claim — are NOT duplicates. Cites the contracted per-side rate and/or proof the counterpart claim already paid. Use when a duplicate/5AF/paid-to-another-provider denial is really a billing-structure misunderstanding, not an actual duplicate.
archetypes.body:
To Whom It May Concern:

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}

We are writing to request a formal appeal and reprocessing of Claim #{{Claim.Number}}. The following line item(s) were incorrectly denied as duplicate services / paid to another provider: {{Claim.CPT}}.

[CHOOSE THE APPLICABLE SCENARIO AND DELETE THE OTHER:]

[SCENARIO A — Co-surgeon claim, per-surgeon-per-side contract:] Under our specific provider contract with {{Payer.Name}}, our practice operates on a per-surgeon, per-side billing model for complex microsurgical breast reconstruction (CPT {{Claim.CPT}}). Per the payer's own instructions, we do not use co-surgeon modifier 62; instead, we bill exclusively with side-specific modifiers (LT/RT). {{Provider.Name}} is the [primary / counterpart] surgeon for the [left/right] side; {{CoSurgeon.Name}} submitted a separate claim for the [other] side under this exact same billing structure[, and was paid $[FILL IN amount] by {{Payer.Name}} on [FILL IN date] under Claim #[FILL IN]]. {{Provider.Name}}'s claim represents the counterpart surgeon charge for the same surgery and must be honored under the same contractual terms.
Contracted Rate: Our contracted rate for the primary side ({{Claim.CPT}}-[LT/RT]) is $[FILL IN], and for the assisting/counterpart side is $[FILL IN].

[SCENARIO B — PA/assistant billed under main surgeon, confused with co-surgeon payment:] {{Assistant.Name}} actively assisted the primary surgeon, {{Provider.Name}}, during this complex operative session. Because {{Assistant.Name}} is not independently credentialed to bill {{Payer.Name}} directly, the assistant-at-surgery services were appropriately submitted under the supervising physician with the -AS modifier appended. This submission complies with {{Payer.Name}}'s billing rules for non-credentialed physician assistants acting as surgical assistants. Upon review, these lines were improperly flagged as duplicate services based on prior payments already made to the primary co-surgeons. This is not a duplicate: co-surgeon reimbursement covers the distinct surgical work executed by the lead surgeons, while the charges appended with modifier -AS represent the separate, hands-on, medically necessary assistant-at-surgery services provided by {{Assistant.Name}} during the same operation.

archetypes.name: PR-204 / Generic Non-Covered Denial — Demand for Specific Plan Language
archetypes.summary: An aggressive, burden-shifting rebuttal for when a payer issues a bare PR-204 ("not covered under current benefit plan") or similarly generic denial with no CPT-specific explanation. Walks through the operative complexity in detail, then explicitly demands the payer cite the exact plan/policy provision, exclusion, or benefit limitation for EACH denied CPT code — putting the burden of specificity back on the payer. Especially effective for multi-CPT claims and complex/sensitive procedures.
archetypes.body:
Dear Appeals Committee / Claims Reviewer,

Patient: {{Patient.Name}} (Member ID {{Patient.MemberID}})
Claim #: {{Claim.Number}}  |  CPT {{Claim.CPT}}  |  Date of Service: {{Claim.ServiceDate}}
Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of CPT code(s) {{Claim.CPT}} for services performed by {{Provider.Name}} on {{Claim.ServiceDate}} at [FILL IN facility]. We are appealing the denial of these services under claim {{Claim.Number}}. The claim was issued a denial under adjustment code [FILL IN, e.g. PR-204], stating that the services are not covered under the patient's current benefit plan. We respectfully request that {{Payer.Name}} conduct a complete reconsideration of this claim based upon the operative report, medical records, the actual services rendered, and the patient's applicable benefit plan.

The submitted operative documentation clearly establishes that the services were performed as part of one complex, medically necessary [FILL IN: procedure type] requiring [FILL IN: operative complexity — dissection, excision, reconstruction, closure technique, etc.]. The operative report documents the substantial complexity of the procedure and the significant surgical work performed:
[FILL IN: detailed operative narrative supporting complexity and necessity]

This was not a cosmetic or convenience procedure, nor was the submitted documentation limited to a superficial or elective office-level service.

The use of [FILL IN denial code] requires clarification because it is a benefit-plan coverage determination. It does not, by itself, establish that the services were incorrectly reported, improperly documented, not medically necessary, experimental, investigational, or incorrectly coded.

Accordingly, if {{Payer.Name}} maintains that these services are excluded from coverage, we respectfully request that {{Payer.Name}} provide in its written determination:
• The exact provision of the patient's benefit plan that excludes each denied CPT code.
• The specific benefit category or contractual exclusion relied upon for each code individually.
• The applicable policy, medical policy, Certificate/Evidence of Coverage provision, or other controlling plan language in effect on the date of service.
• An explanation of whether the denial is based on a specific exclusion, a benefit limitation, a coding issue, medical-policy criteria, or another contractual provision.
• If only a portion of the services is excluded, identification of the specific service and corresponding CPT code to which the exclusion applies, along with confirmation that the submitted operative report and medical records were reviewed in their entirety.

A generic denial does not adequately explain the contractual basis for nonpayment when extensive medical records and operative documentation have been submitted. We ask {{Payer.Name}} to review the claim based upon the actual clinical circumstances and the patient's specific plan language rather than relying solely upon a generic adjustment code.

[IF APPLICABLE: The record further documents the need for a qualified surgical assistant. [FILL IN: assistant's role and why one was necessary].]

Based upon the complete operative documentation, we respectfully request that {{Payer.Name}} overturn the denial, reconsider CPT {{Claim.CPT}} individually, and reprocess the claim for payment according to the patient's applicable benefits and the provider's contractual terms. We further request review by an appropriately qualified clinical/medical reviewer and, where applicable, a benefits/contractual specialist, so that both the clinical documentation and the contractual coverage issue are appropriately evaluated.

Thank you for your prompt and thorough review. We expect a formal redetermination within standard appeal timelines. For any immediate clinical or administrative inquiries regarding this appeal, contact {{Sender.Name}} directly at {{Sender.Email}} or {{Sender.Phone}}.

archetypes.name: Modifier 59 — Distinct Procedural Service (Clean Bundling Rebuttal)
archetypes.summary: A lighter, cleaner version of the bundling dispute for when two related CPT codes (e.g. a revision code and an implant/prosthesis code) are denied as mutually inclusive, but the operative report documents genuinely separate, non-incidental work. Rendering Provider: {{Provider.Name}}  |  NPI: {{Provider.NPI}}

The operative report identifies the following procedures as performed:
[FILL IN: procedure 1]
[FILL IN: procedure 2]
[FILL IN: procedure 3 — list each distinct component from the operative note]

In addition to [FILL IN: the bundled/incidental-seeming procedure], {{Provider.Name}} performed substantial additional work involving [FILL IN: anatomical detail]. The [FILL IN: revision/additional] procedures were medically necessary due to [FILL IN: patient history and clinical rationale].

cptRationale.title: Microsurgical Autologous Breast Reconstruction (DIEP/TRAM/Perforator Flap)
cptRationale.body: This claim involves microsurgical, autologous breast reconstruction (free or perforator flap technique) performed as a staged component of post-mastectomy reconstructive care — a service category subject to the coverage mandates of the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act (WHCRA) of 1998, which requires group health plans and issuers that cover mastectomy to also cover reconstruction of the breast on which the mastectomy was performed, surgery on the other breast to produce a symmetrical appearance, and treatment of physical complications at all stages, including lymphedema. Autologous flap reconstruction (DIEP, TRAM, or other perforator/free-flap technique) is a recognized, medically necessary reconstructive modality — not a cosmetic enhancement — supported by the operative report's documentation of flap harvest, microvascular anastomosis, and reconstructive intent. [DESCRIBE: mastectomy date/type, laterality, and any prior failed implant-based reconstruction or radiation history supporting the choice of autologous technique].

cptRationale.chargeGroupLabel: Breast Reconstruction — Revision, Expander & Implant Stages
cptRationale.title: Breast Reconstruction Revision / Tissue Expander / Implant Exchange
cptRationale.body: This claim involves a revision, tissue-expander, or implant-exchange stage of post-mastectomy breast reconstruction — services that fall squarely within the reconstructive continuum protected under the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act (WHCRA) rather than elective or cosmetic revision surgery. CPT codes in this group describe surgical correction of a complication of prior breast reconstruction, including but not limited to asymmetry requiring surgical correction, capsular contracture, flap or implant malposition, contour irregularity causing functional or symptomatic compromise, or a partial reconstructive failure. [DESCRIBE: specific clinical indication for this revision stage — e.g. capsular contracture grade, documented asymmetry, expander-to-implant exchange timeline, flap complication]. This is corrective, reconstructive surgery performed to remedy a documented complication of a covered reconstructive procedure, not an elective cosmetic enhancement.

cptRationale.title: Breast Reduction & Post-Bariatric Contouring
cptRationale.body: This claim involves reduction mammaplasty or post-bariatric body contouring (excisional lipectomy) performed to correct a documented functional impairment — chronic neck, shoulder, or back pain; intertriginous skin breakdown/rash; shoulder-strap grooving; or panniculus-related functional limitation and recurrent infection — rather than for cosmetic contouring alone. Medical necessity for these procedures is customarily established through a combination of: (1) documented symptom duration and severity, (2) a failed trial of conservative management (physical therapy, supportive garments, dermatologic treatment of intertrigo), and (3) for reduction mammaplasty, a resection-weight estimate consistent with the Schnur sliding scale or the payer's own published gram-per-breast threshold. [DESCRIBE: symptom history, conservative treatment attempted and duration, and estimated/actual resection weight or excised specimen weight].

cptRationale.title: Mastectomy & Nipple-Areola Reconstruction
cptRationale.body: This claim involves mastectomy or nipple-areola complex reconstruction performed as a defined stage of the WHCRA-protected reconstructive continuum following mastectomy for breast cancer, a BRCA/genetic risk-reducing indication, or a covered gender-affirming indication. Nipple-areola reconstruction and tattooing are recognized final stages of breast reconstruction, not standalone cosmetic procedures, and are medically necessary to complete the reconstructive result following a covered mastectomy. [DESCRIBE: mastectomy indication (oncologic, risk-reducing, or gender-affirming), date, and stage of reconstruction this claim represents].
guidelineHooks: NCCN breast cancer risk-reduction guidelines (where prophylactic)

cptRationale.chargeGroupLabel: Adjacent Tissue Transfer & Complex Wound Closure
cptRationale.title: Adjacent Tissue Transfer & Complex Wound Closure
cptRationale.body: This claim involves adjacent tissue transfer and/or complex wound closure performed to achieve durable coverage of a surgical or traumatic defect that could not be safely closed by simple or intermediate repair. The operative complexity underlying the closure technique billed — undermining, rotation/advancement flap design, and layered closure to relieve tension over the defect — is the clinical and coding basis for the code level billed, distinct from a simple linear repair. [DESCRIBE: defect size/location, why simple or intermediate repair was not clinically adequate, and the specific flap/closure technique performed per the operative note].
guidelineHooks: CPT/AMA coding definitions for tissue transfer vs. simple/intermediate repair

cptRationale.title: Gender-Affirming Genital Reconstruction
cptRationale.body: This claim involves gender-affirming genital reconstruction performed as part of a physician-directed treatment plan for gender dysphoria, consistent with the WPATH (World Professional Association for Transgender Health) Standards of Care, Version 8, criteria for surgical readiness — including persistent, well-documented gender dysphoria; capacity to consent; and, where applicable under the payer's own medical policy, the required duration of hormone therapy and/or real-life experience. Under the No Surprises Act's and Section 1557's nondiscrimination provisions and prevailing payer medical-necessity policy for gender-affirming care, coverage determinations for this service category must apply the same individualized medical-necessity review used for comparable non-gender-affirming reconstructive procedures — a categorical denial of a WPATH-indicated procedure as 'cosmetic' does not reflect an individualized review. [DESCRIBE: WPATH criteria satisfied — referral letters, hormone therapy duration, and any prior authorization already on file].

cptRationale.title: Craniofacial / Facial Reconstruction
cptRationale.body: This claim involves craniofacial or facial reconstructive surgery performed to correct a functional deficit or a congenital, traumatic, or post-oncologic structural defect. The operative documentation on file — including the specific structural/functional deficit addressed (nasal airway obstruction, orbital/globe malposition, mandibular asymmetry affecting occlusion, or a congenital craniofacial anomaly) — distinguishes this service from an elective cosmetic facial procedure. [DESCRIBE: the specific functional deficit corrected, its etiology (congenital/traumatic/post-oncologic), and any objective functional testing (e.g. nasal airflow study, occlusal analysis) supporting necessity].
guidelineHooks: ASPS reconstructive-vs-cosmetic criteria for craniofacial surgery

cptRationale.title: Skin Grafting & Surgical Wound Debridement
cptRationale.body: This claim involves skin grafting and/or surgical wound debridement performed to manage a documented non-healing wound (surgical, traumatic, pressure-related, or diabetic/vascular in etiology). The depth and extent of debridement billed (partial/full-thickness skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, muscle, or bone) and the graft type billed (split-thickness autograft, full-thickness autograft, or skin substitute) are supported by the operative and wound-measurement documentation on file, consistent with CPT/CMS coding guidance requiring debridement depth and total wound surface area to be separately documented in the operative note. [DESCRIBE: wound etiology, measured depth/surface area, and graft or debridement type performed per the operative note].
guidelineHooks: CMS wound-care LCD depth/measurement documentation standards

cptRationale.title: Evaluation & Management Encounter
cptRationale.body: This claim involves a medically necessary evaluation and management encounter directly related to the patient's surgical episode of care — pre-operative clearance/consultation, post-operative complication management, or a new/separately identifiable problem addressed during a global period — and is appropriately billed with the corresponding E/M modifier (e.g. modifier 24 or 25) where applicable. CMS global-surgery guidance permits separate E/M reimbursement where the visit addresses a concern unrelated to, or a complication that requires additional management beyond, the routine post-operative course bundled into the surgical global fee. [DESCRIBE: reason for the visit, whether it is unrelated to the global surgical episode or a complication requiring additional management, and the modifier appended].
guidelineHooks: CMS global-surgery period E/M carve-out guidance

denialRationale.title: Non-Covered / Categorized as Cosmetic or Excluded
denialRationale.body: Regulatory and Coding Basis for Coverage: The applicable ICD-10 diagnosis code(s) submitted with this claim — {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} — establish the underlying medical condition necessitating this procedure and directly support medical necessity independent of any cosmetic or elective classification. Where the denied service falls within a payer medical-necessity policy rather than a categorical plan exclusion, {{Payer.Name}}'s own coverage determination guidelines require individualized review against the submitted diagnosis and operative findings, not a blanket non-covered code. This claim was contracted at {{Claim.ContractedRate}} under the provider's participation agreement with {{Payer.Name}}; a denial that disregards the contracted fee schedule and the clinical documentation on file is inconsistent with both the payer's medical policy and the terms of that agreement. We request that {{Payer.Name}} identify, in writing, the specific plan provision, policy, or coding edit relied upon if any portion of this claim remains denied.

denialRationale.title: NCCI Bundling / Mutually Inclusive Denial
denialRationale.body: NCCI and Bundling Analysis: The National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) procedure-to-procedure edits published by CMS permit separate reporting of distinct, medically necessary services performed at different anatomic sites, through separate incisions, or during a distinct operative session, when appended with the appropriate modifier and supported by documentation — as is the case here. Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} documented in the operative note support that the bundled component represents a separately identifiable service, not an inherent, always-included step of the primary procedure. Modifier 59 (or the applicable X{E,S,P,U} modifier) was appropriately appended to indicate that these services were distinct and separately identifiable. We request confirmation of the specific NCCI edit pair and modifier indicator relied upon, and reprocessing of the separately reportable component at the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}}.

denialRationale.title: Prior Authorization Dispute
denialRationale.body: Authorization and Medical Necessity Alignment: {{Payer.Name}}'s own utilization-management criteria require prior authorization determinations to be based on the clinical information submitted at the time of request. Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} match the clinical indication reviewed and approved (or, if no authorization was on file, establish medical necessity independent of the authorization requirement) under CMS medical-necessity standards applicable to this class of reconstructive/surgical service. Prior Authorization #{{Claim.AuthNumber}}, where obtained, was properly requested and the date of service falls within the approved coverage window. A denial on authorization grounds does not relieve {{Payer.Name}} of its obligation to pay the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} once the authorization defect is resolved or shown immaterial to the medical necessity of the service rendered.

denialRationale.title: Timely Filing Dispute
denialRationale.body: Timely Filing Basis: Per {{Payer.Name}}'s provider manual and the terms of the provider's participation agreement, the timely filing clock runs from the later of the date of service or the date a clean claim could first be submitted, and is tolled during any period the claim was pending additional information, corrected and resubmitted, or affected by a payer system/portal error. [FILL IN: date of original submission and any confirmation number, fax confirmation, or clearinghouse acceptance report evidencing timely submission]. There is a material distinction between unsubmitted records/claims and records submitted but unindexed by the payer; we request that {{Payer.Name}} conduct an internal document-management search using the confirmation ID(s) cited to verify the exact date and time the transmission entered the payer's system. Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} and the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} on file for this service are unaffected by the filing dispute and should govern reprocessing once timely filing is confirmed.

denialRationale.title: Eligibility, Benefit Cap, or Underpayment Dispute
denialRationale.body: Benefit and Contract Verification: Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} document the covered clinical condition underlying this service. Where {{Payer.Name}} has verified active eligibility for the date of service {{Claim.ServiceDate}}, a denial citing exhausted or unavailable benefits must specify the exact benefit category, annual/lifetime maximum, or plan provision applied, and confirm whether a separate, lower cosmetic-service cap was mistakenly applied to a reconstructive or medically necessary service. Where the dispute is instead an underpayment relative to the fee schedule — including a bilateral service billed with modifier 50 that was not priced at the standard 150% bilateral allowance — we request a line-by-line contracted-rate reconciliation and reprocessing to the full contracted amount of {{Claim.ContractedRate}}.

denialRationale.title: Coding / Place-of-Service Dispute
denialRationale.body: Coding and Regulatory Alignment: The CPT and ICD-10 code sets submitted — including diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} — are consistent with current CMS/AMA coding guidance and correctly reflect the procedure(s) performed and documented in the operative report. Where the denial cites an invalid place-of-service determination, the CMS Physician Fee Schedule's non-facility relative value unit (RVU) for this CPT explicitly recognizes that the code may be safely and appropriately performed in the billed setting, and any active prior authorization on file (Auth #{{Claim.AuthNumber}}) confirms utilization-management protocols were satisfied before service delivery. Where {{Payer.Name}}'s medical policy or coding-edit software flagged a code-pair, units, or diagnosis-procedure mismatch instead, we request identification of the specific edit relied upon; the operative documentation on file supports the codes as billed. This claim is contracted at {{Claim.ContractedRate}}, which should govern reprocessing once the coding question is resolved.

denialRationale.title: Duplicate-Claim / Co-Surgeon / Assistant-Surgeon Billing Dispute
denialRationale.body: Billing Accuracy Review: The claim as submitted reflects the services actually rendered and documented for diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}}, billed at the provider's contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} under the current participation agreement with {{Payer.Name}}. If this denial reflects a duplicate-claim system match, we confirm this submission corresponds to a single, distinct date of service and procedure — not a duplicate of any previously adjudicated claim. Where the claim reflects a co-surgeon (per-surgeon, per-side, modifier LT/RT) or assistant-at-surgery (modifier -AS, non-credentialed PA billed under the supervising physician) billing structure already validated by {{Payer.Name}}'s payment of the counterpart claim for the same operative session, that payment establishes the plan's own acceptance of medical necessity, coverage, and the contractual billing structure for this encounter — refusing to reimburse the distinct counterpart or assistant charge for the identical session is inconsistent with that prior determination. We request removal of the duplicate flag and reprocessing under the contracted terms.

denialRationale.title: Additional/Missing Medical Records Dispute
denialRationale.body: Clinical Documentation on File: The enclosed operative report, progress notes, and diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} constitute the complete medical record supporting this claim and directly respond to {{Payer.Name}}'s request for clinical documentation. Under standard payer clinical-review guidelines, a complete operative report paired with the corroborating ICD-10 diagnosis is sufficient to establish medical necessity without further supplementation absent a specific, itemized deficiency. Where records were previously submitted via the provider portal or clearinghouse, {{Payer.Name}}'s inability to locate or index previously transmitted documentation within its internal system does not constitute a failure to submit by the provider, and we request an internal document-management search using the submission confirmation ID(s) on file. We request reprocessing at the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} based on the records now (re-)submitted, or a written itemization of any information still considered deficient.

denialRationale.title: NPI Mismatch / Non-Participating / Out-of-Network Dispute
denialRationale.body: Network and Credentialing Status: The rendering/billing NPI on this claim is affiliated with {{Practice.NPI}} under the provider's active participation agreement with {{Payer.Name}}, which establishes the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} for this service — the rendering provider is not, in fact, out-of-network or non-participating, and any credentialing-database record suggesting otherwise should be corrected. Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} document the covered clinical condition. Where a No Surprises Act protection applies (e.g., emergency services or ancillary care at an in-network facility, per 45 CFR 149.110), the claim must be processed at the in-network cost-sharing level regardless of any credentialing-database mismatch. Where the claim instead reflects an assistant-at-surgery or non-credentialed PA billed under the main surgeon's NPI, {{Payer.Name}}'s payment of the primary surgeon's claim for this identical operative session already validates the medical necessity and contractual coverage of the encounter as a whole.

denialRationale.title: Contracted-Rate Discrepancy / Underpayment
denialRationale.body: Contracted Rate Discrepancy: Per the provider's participation agreement with {{Payer.Name}}, the contracted allowable for CPT {{Claim.CPTCode}} on the applicable fee schedule is {{Claim.ContractedRate}}. The remittance for this claim reflects an amount inconsistent with that contracted rate for diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} and the documented service level — including, where applicable, a bilateral service billed with modifier 50 that was not priced at the standard 150% bilateral allowance. We request an itemized fee-schedule reconciliation confirming the correct contracted allowable and reprocessing of any underpayment identified, consistent with the terms of the current agreement.

denialRationale.title: Medical Necessity Dispute
denialRationale.body: Medical Necessity Basis: The enclosed operative report and diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} document the clinical findings, functional impairment, and/or failed conservative management supporting medical necessity for this service, consistent with CMS medical-necessity standards and, where applicable, the specialty-specific clinical-guideline criteria referenced in the CPT Rationale section above. A denial that recharacterizes a clinically indicated, guideline-supported procedure as cosmetic or investigational without addressing the submitted clinical documentation does not reflect the individualized review {{Payer.Name}}'s own medical policy requires. We request that any physician reviewer with relevant specialty expertise re-review the enclosed operative report and clinical documentation against the specific medical-necessity criteria relied upon, and reprocess this claim at the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}}.

denialRationale.title: No Determination Issued / Payer Non-Response
denialRationale.body: Escalation Basis: This claim was submitted on [FILL IN: submission date] and, as of the date of this letter, no written determination — approval, denial, or request for additional information — has been issued by {{Payer.Name}} within its own published claims-processing timeline. Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} and the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} on file establish that this is a clean, adjudicable claim. Under {{Payer.Name}}'s provider manual and applicable state prompt-pay requirements, failure to issue a timely determination does not extend the payer's own processing deadline or prejudice the provider's right to appeal; we request immediate processing and issuance of a written determination, or confirmation that this claim has in fact already been determined and simply not communicated to the provider.

denialRationale.title: Claim Stalled in Adjudication / No Determination Issued
denialRationale.body: Status and Escalation Basis: This claim was submitted on [FILL IN: submission date] and remains in an unresolved 'in process' status beyond {{Payer.Name}}'s own published claims-processing timeline under the applicable provider manual and state prompt-pay requirements. Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} and the contracted rate of {{Claim.ContractedRate}} on file establish that this is a clean, adjudicable claim with no outstanding information request from {{Payer.Name}} on record. We request immediate adjudication and, if a formal determination has already issued but was not received by the provider, a duplicate copy of that determination along with the confirmed issue date so the applicable appeal window is not prejudiced by a payer-side delay.

denialRationale.title: Missing/Invalid Referral Dispute
denialRationale.body: Referral and Network-Pathway Basis: [FILL IN: referring provider name/NPI and referral date, if a referral was in fact obtained]. Where a valid referral was on file at the time of service but not properly linked to this claim during adjudication, we request that {{Payer.Name}} re-associate the referral on file and reprocess accordingly. Where the plan design does not, in fact, require a referral for this service category (e.g. a self-referred specialist service, or a plan without a gatekeeper requirement), we request confirmation of the specific plan provision requiring a referral for CPT {{Claim.CPTCode}} under this member's benefit plan. Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} independently establish medical necessity for the service rendered, and the claim is contracted at {{Claim.ContractedRate}}.

denialRationale.title: Other / Not Otherwise Categorized
denialRationale.body: Diagnosis code(s) {{Claim.DiagnosisCodes}} and the enclosed clinical documentation directly support the medical necessity and correct reporting of this service, and the claim is contracted at {{Claim.ContractedRate}} under the provider's participation agreement with {{Payer.Name}}. We request that {{Payer.Name}} identify, in writing, the specific plan provision, policy, or coding edit relied upon for this denial, and reprocess the claim once that basis is addressed by the documentation on file.
